tl;dr - [strike]skill issue[/strike]If you never played RoR1 or feel adamant on game being fine as is, it's not a bad way to visit the original - shiny graphics, amazing music and the game somewhat feels the same.
If you want certified RoR experience of brain-damage inducing visual diarrhea, insatiable lust for power loaded with new stuff and you like looping the game - buy original RoR1 and download Starstorm mod instead - it feels like a proper "love letter to community" and revisit that I and probably some people expected to see. Even you want to play vanilla, you’ll still get a great way to customize or change your runs with the settings it provides.
 
"Risk of Rain... again" feels like better fitting name.
Same (mostly) game with duct-taped additions in a pretty wrap. I hoped it would be akin to Binding of Isaac: Rebirth, but it is pretty much just a visual update, so it IS my fault for expecting anything else.
It honestly feels like most of development time was spent on these stupid trials, because the rest on the game can't decide if it tries to be better version of original or sledgehammer your balls on any given occasion. 

Visuals are great, some changes like Infusion sprite are odd, but it's no biggie. The music is just as good as it was back then - still carries the whole game, and in higher quality too! God bless Chris, especially for credit rolls.
 
Tele sequences are much better now that you don’t have to fullclear the level. Stage navigation is still pain. The same dilemma of choosing between x1 zoom and melting your eyes for better navigation, or playing on x2 and enjoying new animations at the cost of taking ages to find teleporter.
Some of the stage variations are borrowed from Starstorm, which is a nice detail.

Mountain Shrines are now in RoR1, but they’re way more brutal, and given the adds from Elite Boss get the affix for free, I’d recommend to just ignore them – ‘tis not “we hit all the funny shrines” angle, sadly. Artifact of Prestige is a death sentence, which is a shame. (can be somewhat fun with Command) 

Movement somehow feels jankier and less responsive than original. I assume it has something to do with changes to allow move while shooting, because I only had this problem with auto-attacks/charge/continuous skills - you CAN still jumpshoot-change direction with instant skills like mando's FMJ and so on. Some of the characters are given “ice skates”, that let them preserve high speed after using movement ability and jumping (like bhop, but you gradually lose speed). This allows to mostly circumvent level traversal (Pilot with Aerobatics being the biggest offender), which creates a nasty predicament in the game where every minute is on the line. It also makes characters who can’t do this feel like trash. Artificer is also in the game, but she gives me brain aneurysm – she’s nothing like RoR2’s version and feels more like a skill playtesting afterthought.

Providence Trials are dragging playtime for no real reason other than faster skill unlocks, since the menial tasks that act as alternative would take forever in comparison. Some of the pure combat trials were pretty fun to explore, so credit where credit is due.
[spoiler]Judgement Trial gauntlet itself was pretty good. But static nature of the waves and items for ALL characters reduces it into doing exactly the same thing on different skill sets. Fifteen. Times. No deviations. Aside from Engineer and Drifter, where instead of grabbing Stopwatch you go Amethyst.[/spoiler]
 
Enemies have been rebalanced for less health and more damage to make the game flow better, yet with some of new enemy additions and elites being deadlier than ever, you’ll most likely kite even more lol
Looping is much harder to the point it's not worth doing 99% of the time. You're flooded by spawns almost non-stop the moment you return back, and without proper defenses and damage you'll get deleted for a single slip up.
The game did introduce a good chunk of powerful items that let you scale further (and technically giving a source of i-frames for everyone with Prophet's Cape), but RNG is RNG, and “catching up” is a daunting task in this game. 
 
Multiplayer accessibility is vastly improved, but the multiplayer sessions get messy with desyncing and constant fear of game randomly ending out of blue. You also can't ping stuff, why? Starstorm mod for RoR1 had this function and it helped even in single player - why is it not here...? You even have people who worked on that mod.
 
Overall, I’m still confused what was the intention with RoR:R in the end. Was the game supposed to be faster? Slower? A new framework to revitalise the original? Because the game kinda fails in all of that.
Some of the issues are baffling, especially given more than half a year of delay. (like skill descriptions not maching up the numbers in game).
And now that Hoopo is aquired by Valve, the game may as well be in the same state RoR1 was - no news on that promised "modding" support. Or any news, for that matter.
 
Time really is a flat circle, huh?

[b] Risk of Rain Returns was featured on my YouTube channel[/b]




https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3100987813


and now onto the short review

[h1]TL;DR Review[/h1]




//intro//

Hello, MF Kraven here- and welcome to a less than 10 mins review. A YouTube series where I take a look at niche titles, hidden gems & often overlooked games & tell you whether or not you should buy it, in less than 10 mins. So if that is the type of content that you like, consider subscribing, & liking this video.

Today I take a look at Risk of Rain Returns, a remastering & re-tweaked version of Risk of Rain an action platformer with roguelike elements. players will have to play their best to get as far as possible. Fight on a mysterious planet with randomly spawning enemies and bosses, either alone or with 3 friends in online co-op. One of my favorite games from 2013-  but will the 2D version still hold up 10 years later especially when Risk of Rain 2 has been out since 2020? Let's find out! 

//Graphics, Sound & Artstyle//

Taking the beautiful pixel art cell shaded combination that comes together like an orgasm for the eye, it's safe to say I am very much a fan of it & then you accompany this with a serene soundtrack, girthy sfx for weapons and damage inflicted. It's absolutely perfect 


//Gameplay//

You immediately spawn into a world not known to you in a random location. There you must look for a portal that can take you to the next world but not before defeating a random BOSS, and unto the next until you meet the antagonist of the game. But it's the journey not the destination that makes the repetitive formula in Risk of Rain not only rewarding but fun.

See each survivor has 4 unique abilities/weapons that they can use on enemies. But the items you pickup affect the gameplay loop entirely- so if you're not a fan of RNG, you might already be tuning out. It's in these items that can make your run that much easier or harder. Scattered around each map you play are vending machines, chests, & statues you can buy with coins or sometimes blood- that will give you items or nothing at all. For example, you may pickup an item that will heal you if you hit an opponent, another one speeds your character up, one makes fungi grow when you're standing still to heal you, one gives you the ability to jump twice & yes all of the items are stackable so ive had a build that had me be able to jump 5 times in the air, shoot random missiles & anyone near me would take damage as an electri current ran through my body. There are over 130 items to pick up or use, giving you almost endless possibilities

There are 15 characters that they call survivors available to pick from- 3 more than Risk of Rain with most of them being locked but easily attainable through playing.

A new game mode called Providence Trials where you can unlock abilities for your survivors & the game also keeps extensive track of your stats.




//Price//

 14.99 USD


//How many hours estimated//

I'm about 7 hours in, & haven't unlocked much- getting reuse to the controls- but honestly see myself sinking 20 hours in.

//Is it Playable on Steamdeck?//

Yes! Although the UI is way smaller, it's still very much enjoyable & after playing for around 2 hours- my battery life was barely impacted.



//Final Thoughts//

Taking it back to the 2D mechanic that plays like a platformer but with pizazz. And yeah, I swore on my mama that I would be done with platformers, yet here we are, sorry mama. Risk of Rain Returns captures 
my imagination and frustration like Risk of Rain 2 just couldn't and i really liked the 3D iteration of Risk of Rain.

The rush of feeling invincible only to be humbled in the next level, searching through familiar looking stages with completely random drops & when the stars align and I get a ton of my favorite power-ups man someone call the police cause it's criminal how much of a good time i'm having, managing an escape plan that would have me circle back like a complete scumbag, and getting those crits with Bandit to refresh my abilities- and I get all that serotonin from this minimalist rogue-lite shooter platformer. 


Then you add Providence Trials which are challenges that can help you unlock abilities for your survivors, changing up one of their abilities is refreshing fun- normally i don't even bother with these mini-game type of chall a map asap. But fret not, if these challenges aren't your cup of tea & you want to unlock other abilities? Well the devs also put in a feature that allows you to for example defeat a certain amount of enemies in playthroughs or pass certain amount of levels with a survivor- i really like that


Before finding out this remake was coming I felt nostalgic & tried playing the OG with a friend online, only to just be frustrated trying to connect online, then we just stopped trying & went on to play D&D Lords of Waterdeep or something. But now? It's a feature to play online & it's a breeze.


Based on everything i've been saying, as much praise as I give it, let me just warn you. This is one of thee most difficult games I've ever played. Maybe I'm a masochist, maybe John Cena's mantra of Never Give Up has stuck with me, but I always go in for more... so if getting your ass handed to you by pixels isn't for you? Skip it. For everyone else?




[h1]Buy it Now![/h1]

A rare example of a perfect remaster, Risk of Rain Returns lives up to the original and pushes the original concept even further. The game perfectly balances new additions (including some of Risk of Rain 2) and quality of life improvements with a freshly painted game with visual improvements across the board. In the many hours I've played the only thing I've had a complaint about is that items get lost in the action a little when your zoomed out, but that single complaint is outweighed by the hours upon hours of fun this game offers and the enjoyment returning fans and newcomers alike will get from the experience. If you liked RoR2 or RoR original, you will like this game. If you have never played the series before this is a brilliant place to start, and it never hurts to have some friends along for the ride. [b]The Short: An absolute treat for Risk of Rain 1 fans, and an intensely fun curiosity for the Risk of Rain 2 fans it clicks with[/b]

The Long:

Risk of Rain 1 was one of the foundational stepping stones of the modern day roguelike genre that now seems like a titan in and of itself among the indie game scene, so going back to it today is a little bit dated, as most games that tried this formula early on are. But if you enjoyed Risk of Rain 1 or, like me, were a little obsessed with it, good news! Risk of Rain Returns is exactly what you want; more characters, more content, more modern convenience, but you'll still bash things against walls and wade into clustered groups of enemy sprites, hoping you don't die in the overlap as you mash buttons and stack your 10th crowbar.

To the Risk of Rain 2 fans on the fence about this game; there's no major changes in the formula. The biggest worries you'll have are adjusting to the difference in gameplay from 3D to 2D. You'll essentially have to go in reverse from what old fans did when Risk 2 came out. There's a little bit of MoBa in this iteration of the game, with more precise control needed over cooldowns and builds, which was the style at the time. There are quirks you can learn to work around to make the game fun, and this remake makes it simpler than ever to adjust the experience to your preferred level of hand holding; No one is going to care if you play the RoR remake on Drizzle. You can unlock everything just fine.

One entirely new addition worth pointing out is the Providence Trials; a grid of specific, seeded scenarios that task you with doing a specific challenge... Like shooting down 30 enemies in 3 minutes, or surviving with only 1 hp. Usually you'll have alternative skills, which are also unlocked through this mode... But for people who hate having to go through with this "smash bros event board' style unlock process, every ability in the game can also be unlocked by an alternate grind. The remastered soundtrack, phenomenal and electric in its own right, has been joined by a handful of remixes that make your shootout with an encroaching hoard of aliens all the more pulse pounding. The graphics are sharper and utterly gorgeous pixel art that might make you glance twice at Risk of Rain's 3D transition.

The above is just a handful of the added features to entice you if you're worried there's enough here to warrant a purchase of a remake, whether you're a returning fan or a new one. So long as you're aware of the slightly rusty nature underneath the modern padding, my opinion is that it absolutely is worth it. You probably won't be disappointed, despite a few clunky tagalongs from the past. You're still crashing down, fighting things 50 times your size, and walking away from it all mutated beyond repair... You just get to do it as an adorable tiny sprite now.
